title: Armstrong–Madison: the February outlier
status: No complete, independently verified decipherment established by this review
identity: This workbench examines John Armstrong Jr.'s letter to James Madison from Paris dated 20 February 1808, not the separate coded postscript of 30 August 1808.
method: Primary editorial texts first; discovery services second; pinned secondary files only as comparison inputs. Local measurements are recomputed from the retained text. Tool-fetched extracts are normalized transcriptions/notes, not authenticated HTTP byte captures. No external solver code was executed.

findings.title: The target is 20 February 1808
findings.text: Founders Online prints the Paris date, the clear opening ‘The’, numerical groups interleaved with graphic descriptions, and Armstrong's closing. It identifies the repository as DNA, RG 59, Diplomatic Despatches, France. Graphic placeholders are editorial descriptions, not transcribed shorthand.

findings.title: Secretary of state, not yet president
findings.text: In February 1808 Madison was secretary of state and Armstrong was the U.S. minister plenipotentiary in France. AFIO's labels ‘President’ and ‘Secretary of War’ describe later roles and are anachronistic for this letter. A role error is not by itself a cryptographic disproof.

findings.title: A cipher the office could not find
findings.text: On 10 May Graham reported a letter in Armstrong's packet for which he could find no key. On 15 May Madison called an undeciphered letter from ‘A.’ probably misaddressed and said no such cipher was in the office. Neither note specifies 20 February: identifying that item with the February outlier is a strong contextual inference, not an explicit date match or proof that it was never subsequently decoded.

findings.title: An announcement is not an aligned decipherment
findings.text: AFIO announced Yaacov Apelbaum as its contest winner on 27 May 2025 and published a short maritime paragraph with 56 number-to-word labels. Applying those exact labels in order leaves most of the numerical text unaccounted for, as well as all graphical passages. The viewer preserves every unknown instead of smoothing them into prose.

findings.title: The announcement's reference letters do not supply the key
findings.text: The linked 15 July 1804 letter concerns travel preparations, Hamilton's death and a report about France, not the claimed maritime argument. The linked 7 June 1806 letter does concern the ship Hope and restitution. The latter supplies relevant background, not the missing number-to-word alignment; neither reference authenticates the proposed February plaintext.

findings.title: Editorial numbers are not code groups
findings.text: The retained Founders text has 365 fully printed numeric readings plus one damaged prefix, 17⟨   ⟩. Treating that prefix provisionally as 17 gives 366 readings. A pinned GitHub comparison stream instead has 369: it includes the editorial 2 from ‘2 lines of symbols’ and two editorial 1s from ‘1 line of symbols’. This review does not repeat those three additions as cipher groups.

findings.title: 203 is not silently changed to 1203
findings.text: Founders prints 203 in the fifth numeric line. Cryptiana's tentative reading and the attachment instead suggest 1203; Cryptiana also questions a digit in the opening 1841. The damaged 17 prefix is not an established complete group. Facsimile collation remains necessary before asserting the true manuscript readings.

findings.title: A real parallel is not a proven opening
findings.text: Armstrong's open letter to Jefferson of 15 February 1808 really begins with a recommendation of a bearer as active, sober, industrious and brave. A blog commenter proposes fitting that wording to the February cipher. The parallel is verified, but the proposed numeric assignments, Taylor-shorthand identifications and continuation are not established by that parallel alone. The open letter says ‘man, and…’, not the proposed continuation ‘man of…’.

findings.title: 26 trailing-zero pairs do not establish equivalence
findings.text: The complete editorial readings contain 26 distinct pairs n and 10n. This count is reproducible. It does not show that the paired codes mean the same thing, establish a chance expectation, or justify deleting all final zeros. No null-model significance or system identification is claimed here.

findings.title: Do not substitute the August postscript
findings.text: The Library of Congress and Founders identify a different Armstrong letter dated 30 August 1808. Cryptiana's THE=972 reconstruction and a GitHub near-complete reading concern that postscript. The GitHub reading includes inferred assignments, proposed transcription changes and a final 555→1555 emendation. Those claims have not been independently collated here and do not solve the February letter.

findings.title: Gutenberg and Archive searches produced context
findings.text: A pinned GITenberg copy of Gutenberg ebook 53767 contains Jefferson's letter to Armstrong of 2 May 1808. Direct Gutenberg retrieval failed; the mirror is explicitly identified rather than counted as independent corroboration. Internet Archive supplies an 1865 Madison edition and Taylor's 1786 stenography title. No verified February plaintext or key was recovered from these bounded searches.

findings.title: Imported narrative is not newly certified
findings.text: The original 18 workbench sections remain available. Assertions in its Combined text, piracy, Bastille, Arnold and other historical narratives are not a decipherment and have not all been source-checked in this pass. The new review supersedes unsupported claims about what the encrypted letter is ‘about’. The attachment's icon is artwork, not a manuscript facsimile.

letters.title: John Graham → Madison · 10 May 1808
letters.text: You will find in Genl Armstrongs Packet a Letter written in a Cypher to which we have no Key I beleive in the office, at least none that I can find

letters.title: Madison → Jefferson · 15 May 1808
letters.text: The undecyphered letter from A. was probably misaddressed to the Secretary of State. No such Cypher is in the office, and must be one concerted with another correspondent.

letters.title: Armstrong → Jefferson · 15 February 1808
letters.text: The bearer of this is an active, sober, industreous and brave man, and in the event of a war, may be very usefully employed.

nextSteps.title: Collate the facsimiles
nextSteps.text: Acquire and inspect the UVA originals and NARA M34 roll 14 object pages 29–32. Record page/frame coordinates, 203/1203, 1841, and the damaged prefix. The NARA catalog page was fetched but the direct JPEG returned HTTP 500; no image bytes or complete graphical transcription are bundled.

nextSteps.title: Transcribe graphics without preselecting a shorthand
nextSteps.text: Create a reproducible glyph inventory with crop coordinates and uncertainty alternatives. Compare Taylor 1786, Gurney, Byrom, Mavor and other period systems. Bibliographic existence and visual resemblance are not identification; the 1827 Harding revision postdates the letter.

nextSteps.title: Seek an independent key or retained plaintext
nextSteps.text: Follow Warden, Armstrong and other correspondents' manuscript catalogs. The Warden finding-aid PDF retrieval failed here; no box number, access permission, newly located document or request to an archivist is asserted as this review's own result.

nextSteps.title: Test the recommendation crib on held-out material
nextSteps.text: Publish glyph-to-text alignments, repeated-code constraints and a model capable of explaining the remainder, not just an attractive opening. Do not promote a commenter's partial reading or a fitted phrase to an established plaintext.

nextSteps.title: Require a complete, falsifiable solution
nextSteps.text: Supply an exact source transcription, explicit key/model, ordered rendering of every code and graphic, reasoned emendations and an independent witness or held-out validation. Unmapped or inconvenient occurrences must not simply disappear.
